title: The Alpha Illusion: Reported Alpha from LLM Trading Agents Should Not Be Treated as Deployment Evidence
summary: End-to-end LLM trading agents have moved quickly from research curiosity to a small ecosystem of named systems, including FinCon, FinMem, TradingAgents, FinAgent, QuantAgent, and FLAG-Trader. Several of these report headline Sharpe ratios that would be material if read at face value on a deployment desk, and associated benchmarks such as FinBen report trading-task Sharpe statistics in the same range. The gap between architecture research and deployment claim has been crossed too freely on both sides of the academia--industry divide. We take a position on that gap: reported alpha from end-to-end LLM trading agents should not be treated as deployment evidence. Before such returns can support claims of deployable trading capability, they must survive structural validity tests for temporal integrity, real-world frictions, counterfactual robustness, predictive calibration, numerical execution, and multi-agent disaggregation. Current public evidence cannot yet distinguish robust predictive ability from temporal contamination, unmodeled frictions, short-window Sharpe uncertainty, narrative fitting, and parametric priors. The problem is not only evaluative but structural. Language confidence is not tradable probability, narrative reasoning is not numerical execution, and model priors may become undisclosed implicit factor exposures. We contribute a minimum reporting protocol suite, P1--P6, with tiered applicability by claim strength, and a conservative modular alternative that uses LLMs as auditable information interfaces upstream of independent calibration, risk, and execution modules. Code and reproduction harness: \url{https://github.com/hj1650782738/Trading}.
core_methodology: The paper critically evaluates the reporting and validation standards for end-to-end Large Language Model (LLM) trading agents. It proposes a rigorous set of structural validity tests (temporal integrity, frictions, robustness, calibration, execution, multi-agent disaggregation) that reported returns must pass. It also suggests a conservative modular alternative where LLMs act only as auditable information interfaces upstream of traditional, independent quantitative modules (calibration, risk, execution).
data_sources: The paper implicitly analyzes the reported performance metrics (Sharpe ratios, trading task statistics) derived from various public LLM trading agent benchmarks (e.g., FinCon, FinMem, TradingAgents). The discussion centers on the integrity of the evaluation process rather than novel data sources.
alpha_potential: The paper does not propose a new alpha strategy. Instead, it provides a crucial framework for *validating* any alpha derived from LLM-based agents. Its high practical value lies in preventing the deployment of fraudulent or unstable strategies built on poorly validated LLM outputs. It shifts the focus from narrative performance claims to verifiable, friction-aware numerical execution, which is essential for turning LLM insights into deployable quantitative strategies.
title_cn: Alpha的幻觉：不应将LLM交易代理报告的Alpha视为部署的证据
summary_cn: 本文严厉警告，LLM交易代理报告的高夏普比率不应被视为可部署的交易证据。研究指出了当前评估中的结构性缺陷，如时间污染和叙事拟合。研究人员提出了一套系统的有效性测试标准（P1-P6），并推荐采用模块化方法，即LLM仅作为信息接口，其输出需经过独立的风险和执行模块验证，以确保策略的稳健性和可部署性。

title: PULSE: Generative Phase Evolution for Non-Stationary Time Series Forecasting
summary: Time series forecasting under non-stationarity faces a fundamental tension between capturing stable representations and adapting to distribution shifts. Existing methods implicitly rely on static historical assumptions, leading to a critical failure mode we term Phase Amnesia, where models become blind to the evolving global context. To resolve this, we formalize non-stationary dynamics through three physical hypotheses: wold decomposition, dynamical phase evolution, and heteroscedastic manifold generation. These principles inspire PULSE, a physics-informed, plug-and-play framework adopting a Disentangle--Evolve--Simulate design philosophy. Specifically, PULSE utilizes phase-anchored disentanglement to resolve optimization interference caused by dominant trends, employs a Phase Router to actively generate future trajectories, and introduces Statistic-Aware Mixup (SAM) to ensure robustness against out-of-distribution volatility. Empirically, PULSE enables a simple MLP backbone to achieve state-of-the-art or highly competitive performance across 12 real-world benchmarks. This validates that a correct physics-informed inductive bias is far more critical than raw architectural complexity for non-stationary forecasting. The code is available at: https://github.com/Gemost/PULSE.
core_methodology: PULSE is a physics-informed, plug-and-play forecasting framework built around a 'Disentangle--Evolve--Simulate' design philosophy. It uses phase-anchored disentanglement to separate trends from fluctuations, a Phase Router to generate future trajectories based on dynamical phase evolution, and Statistic-Aware Mixup (SAM) for robustness against volatility shifts. It leverages physical hypotheses (Wold decomposition, dynamical phase evolution) to handle non-stationarity.
data_sources: The paper uses 12 real-world time series benchmarks, which implies financial time series data, although the abstract doesn't specify market data specifically. The methodology is designed for generic non-stationary time series.
alpha_potential: The core strength lies in robustly handling non-stationarity and distribution shifts in time series data, which is the central challenge in financial market forecasting. A model that can accurately navigate evolving market regimes, represented here by 'dynamical phase evolution,' has significant potential for developing adaptive trading strategies, especially those sensitive to structural breaks or high volatility periods.

title: Beyond Sentiment Classification: A Generative Framework for Emotion Intensity Evaluation in Text
summary:
We introduce a novel approach to emotion modeling that shifts the focus from
  identification to evaluation, addressing the limitations of discrete classification in
  applied domains such as finance. By constructing a dataset of emotional intensity
  scores and fine-tuning open-weight generative language models to output continuous
  values from 0-100, we demonstrate a more expressive, generalizable framework for
  sentiment and emotion analysis. Our findings not only outperform classification
  baselines but also reveal surprising generalization capabilities and transfer effects
  to related constructs such as sentiment and arousal. This work contributes to the
  interdisciplinary recontextualization of NLP by introducing emotion intensity
  evaluation as an alternative to classification, arguing that this shift better aligns
  with the needs of domains--such as finance--where the degree of emotional content is
  central to interpretation and decision-making.
core_methodology: Fine-tuning generative language models (LLMs) to output continuous emotion intensity scores (0-100) instead of discrete classification labels, moving beyond traditional sentiment analysis.
data_sources: Textual data (e.g., news articles, social media, earnings call transcripts) that has been scored for emotional intensity (likely annotated or derived from related textual sources).
alpha_potential: This methodology offers a more nuanced tool for analyzing textual data than binary or categorical sentiment. In finance, the *degree* of emotion (fear, excitement, uncertainty) in central bank statements, CEO commentary, or breaking news often contains more predictive power than just the direction of sentiment. This continuous intensity score can be incorporated into predictive models (e.g., regression, portfolio optimization) to forecast short-term volatility, anomalous stock returns, or changes in liquidity preferences, moving beyond simple classification-based alpha factors.
title_cn: 超越情感分类：文本中情绪强度评估的生成式框架
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种利用生成式语言模型输出连续情绪强度评分（0-100）的创新框架，改进了传统的离散情感分类。在金融领域，文本中情绪的“程度”比单纯的方向更具预测力。这一更精细的度量可用于构建更灵敏的阿尔法因子，以更准确地捕捉市场对新闻、财报或监管声明中情绪变化的反应，从而指导交易决策和风险管理。

title: RAGA: Reading-And-Graph-building-Agent for Autonomous Knowledge Graph Construction and Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary:
Existing LLM-driven knowledge graph (KG) construction methods predominantly employ stateless batch processing pipelines, exhibiting structural deficiencies in cross-chunk semantic relation capture, entity disambiguation, and construction process interpretability. These limitations undermine KG quality, retrieval precision, and deployment trust in high-stakes domains.
  We propose RAGA (Reading And Graph-building Agent), an LLM-based autonomous KG construction and retrieval fusion framework. RAGA provides an atomic toolset supporting full KG lifecycle CRUD operations and embeds a Read-Search-Verify-Construct cognitive constraint into a ReAct tool loop. A KG-vector synchronization mechanism enables hybrid symbolic-vector retrieval, while evidence-anchored verification links every knowledge entry to its source text for auditable provenance.
  Preliminary experiments on a subset of the QASPER scientific QA dataset indicate that RAGA's fusion retrieval outperforms zero-shot baselines, with KG integration providing measurable gains in both answer and evidence quality. The framework design and experimental baseline serve as a reference for agent-driven autonomous KG construction.
core_methodology: RAGA is an LLM-based autonomous framework for Knowledge Graph (KG) construction and retrieval, utilizing a ReAct tool loop with cognitive constraints (Read-Search-Verify-Construct) and supporting full KG CRUD operations. It integrates symbolic KG structures with vector databases for hybrid retrieval.
data_sources: The abstract mentions the QASPER scientific QA dataset for preliminary experiments, but the framework is generally applicable to any structured or unstructured textual data that can form a knowledge graph; in finance, this would imply earning call transcripts, news articles, regulatory filings, etc.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in leveraging LLM agents to autonomously structure complex, unstructured information (like textual financial reports or news narratives) into actionable knowledge graphs. This structured knowledge can then be used for advanced sentiment analysis, causal inference between events/entities (e.g., supply chain links, regulatory impacts), or feeding richer context into RAG systems for quantitative signals. High-quality, verifiable knowledge extraction is crucial for reducing noise in alternative data signals.
title_cn: RAGA：用于自主知识图谱构建和检索增强生成的阅读与图谱构建智能体
summary_cn: RAGA框架利用LLM智能体，通过迭代工具调用（ReAct），实现了知识图谱的自主、可验证构建。此框架能将非结构化文本（如研报、新闻）转化为结构化知识，并通过混合符号-向量检索提升信息准确性。这为量化交易提供了更精准、可追溯的事件驱动信号提取和知识增强RAG能力。

title: Learning Multi-Timescale Abstractions for Hierarchical Combinatorial Planning
summary: The combination of exponentially large action spaces, stochastic dynamics, and long-horizon decision-making under limited resources makes Sequential Stochastic Combinatorial Optimization (SSCO) particularly challenging for reinforcement learning. Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) offers a natural decomposition, but it places the high-level policy in a Semi-Markov Decision Process (SMDP) where actions have variable durations, making it difficult to learn a world model that is suitable for planning. We introduce a model-based hierarchical framework for sequential stochastic combinatorial decision-making that directly addresses this issue. Our method combines a latent-space tree-search planner with an SMDP-aware world model for variable-duration decisions. A multi-timescale objective structures the latent dynamics so that transition magnitudes reflect the effective temporal scales of abstract actions, enabling efficient lookahead under adaptive temporal abstraction. We further learn a subgoal-conditioned budget policy jointly with the world model to support context-aware resource allocation. Across challenging SSCO benchmarks, our method outperforms strong baselines.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a model-based Hierarchical Reinforcement Learning (HRL) framework designed for Sequential Stochastic Combinatorial Optimization (SSCO). Key components include a latent-space tree-search planner integrated with an SMDP-aware world model. A critical innovation is the multi-timescale objective that structures latent dynamics based on abstract action temporal scales, facilitating efficient lookahead planning under variable-duration actions. It also learns a subgoal-conditioned budget policy for resource allocation.
data_sources: The method is demonstrated on SSCO benchmarks, which abstract complex decision processes. In a financial context, this approach would apply to sequential, multi-stage decisions where optimization involves significant time horizons and complex resource constraints, such as sequential portfolio rebalancing, optimal execution over multiple trading sessions, or dynamic hedging strategies.
alpha_potential: The primary alpha potential lies in optimizing complex, long-horizon trading decisions that involve inherent trade-offs across different time scales (e.g., high-frequency tactical adjustments vs. long-term structural allocation). The HRL structure naturally handles the inherent semi-Markov nature of many real-world trading events (where decisions happen stochastically over variable durations). By creating efficient temporal abstractions, the model can perform deeper, resource-aware planning for tasks like optimal trade scheduling or complex dynamic asset allocation where current actions have non-trivial, temporally extended consequences.
title_cn: 学习用于分层组合规划的多时间尺度抽象
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于模型的层次强化学习框架，用于解决具有指数级动作空间和随机动态的序列随机组合优化问题。其核心在于引入多时间尺度目标，使抽象动作的时间尺度反映到潜在动力学中，从而支持高效的前视规划。在量化交易中，此框架可应用于需要长期、分层决策和资源管理的场景，如复杂投资组合动态重平衡或多阶段最优执行策略，以应对不同时间尺度上的交易权衡。

title: Empirical evaluation of Time Series Foundation Models for Day-ahead and Imbalance Electricity Price Forecasting in Belgium
summary: Recent advances in Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs) promise zero-shot forecasting capabilities with minimal task-specific training. While these models have shown strong performance across generic benchmarks, their applicability in volatile, complex electricity markets remains underexplored. Addressing this gap, this study provides a systematic empirical evaluation of several TSFMs, specifically Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt (developed by Amazon), and TimesFM 2.5 (provided by Google), for forecasting Belgian day-ahead and imbalance electricity prices. For both considered markets, Chronos-2 in ARX mode produces the most accurate forecasts. Compared with the best ensemble prediction from other machine learning methods, Chronos-2's Mean Absolute Error (MAE) is 5% lower for the day-ahead market. In contrast, the model yields 10% higher MAE predicting imbalance prices across all forecast horizons, except for the two-hour-ahead horizon. Moreover, we find that TSFMs exhibit genuine zero-shot forecasting skills but still struggle under extreme market conditions.
core_methodology: Empirical evaluation of Time Series Foundation Models (TSFMs), specifically Chronos-2 and Chronos-Bolt (Amazon) and TimesFM 2.5 (Google), utilizing zero-shot forecasting capabilities, comparing performance against traditional ML ensembles.
data_sources: Belgian day-ahead and imbalance electricity market price time series data.
alpha_potential: While the immediate application is electricity price forecasting, the methodology tests the zero-shot forecasting capabilities of state-of-the-art TSFMs in a volatile, complex market setting. Successful application of these models to electricity markets suggests potential transferability to other intermittent or complex financial time series where data scarcity or rapid regime change makes traditional supervised learning difficult. The finding that Chronos-2 outperforms ML ensembles for day-ahead forecasts offers a direct template for energy trading operations, though its underperformance in imbalance markets highlights risk factors.
title_cn: 比利时日前及不平衡电价预测中时间序列基础模型的实证评估
summary_cn: 该研究系统评估了Chronos-2等时间序列基础模型在比利时电力市场的零样本预测能力。Chronos-2在日前电价预测中优于传统机器学习方法，但对不平衡电价预测效果不佳。研究对利用先进AI模型进行高波动性、非标准金融时间序列预测提供了经验参考和模型局限性洞察。

title: Artificial Adaptive Intelligence: The Missing Stage Between Narrow and General Intelligence
summary: Between the narrow systems we deploy and the general intelligence we speculate about lies an entire regime of machine behavior that has never received its own name. This monograph argues that this regime is not empty: it is where meta-learning, neural architecture search, AutoML, continual learning, evolutionary computation, and physics-informed modeling have quietly converged on a common principle, namely the steady removal of the human from the loop of parameter specification. We name this regime Artificial Adaptive Intelligence (AAI) and define it operationally: a system exhibits AAI to the extent that it requires no human-specified tunable hyperparameters while maintaining competitive performance across a diverse distribution of tasks. To make the definition quantitative, we introduce an adaptivity index that measures progress along an axis orthogonal to scale, combining the fraction of hyperparameters absorbed by the system with the performance ratio against a task-specialized baseline. We develop the principle of parametric minimality and ground it in the minimum description length framework, showing that the appropriate hyperparameter count is data-determined rather than designer-determined. We then organize the field around three pathways to minimality: data- and task-aware configuration, structural and evolutionary morphing, and in-training self-adaptation. We analyze their stability, convergence, and governance implications, and illustrate them through case studies spanning aerospace design, financial regime detection, turbulence modeling, ecological dynamics, and vision-language systems. The thesis is that the path from ANI to AGI passes through AAI, and that naming this stage changes what we measure, what we build, and what we call a success.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Artificial Adaptive Intelligence (AAI), a regime between Narrow AI and General AI, characterized by systems that eliminate human-specified tunable hyperparameters while maintaining performance across diverse tasks. The core methodology involves defining an 'adaptivity index' to quantify this autonomous configuration capability and exploring pathways like data-aware configuration, structural morphing (evolutionary computation/NAS), and in-training self-adaptation. This framework aims for 'parametric minimality' based on the Minimum Description Length principle.
data_sources: The case studies mentioned include financial regime detection, aerospace design, turbulence modeling, ecological dynamics, and vision-language systems. For finance, the relevant data is the time-series data used for financial regime detection.
alpha_potential: The high potential lies in creating highly robust, self-tuning trading agents. Traditional quantitative strategies often suffer from catastrophic failure when market regimes shift because hyperparameters (e.g., lookback periods, volatility thresholds, optimization settings) are fixed or require manual retraining. A true AAI system could automatically adapt its internal structure and parameterization based on changing market regimes (as suggested by the 'financial regime detection' case study) without human intervention, leading to superior robustness, stability, and potentially extracting alpha across varying market environments (e.g., high vs. low volatility, trend vs. mean-reversion states).
title_cn: 人工适应性智能：狭义智能与通用智能之间的缺失阶段
summary_cn: 该论文提出了人工适应性智能（AAI）概念，强调AI系统自主移除人工可调超参数的能力。这对于量化交易至关重要，因为它直接解决了策略在不同市场环境中超参数敏感性差、易失效的问题。AAI技术有望催生高度鲁棒、能自动适应市场结构变化的交易模型，提高策略的长久稳定性和跨期表现。

title: Informative Graph Structure Learning
summary:
The quality of graph-structured data is fundamental to the success of modern graph analysis techniques such as Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). However, real-world graph data is often suboptimal, suffering from issues such as noise and incomplete connections. Graph Structure Learning (GSL) has emerged as a promising technique that adaptively optimizes node connections. However, we observe that the effectiveness of GSL often comes at the cost of a dramatic expansion in edge count, resulting in significant storage and computational overhead.
  In this work, we reveal that this limitation stems from the prevalent use of similarity-based edge construction, which predominantly connects highly similar neighbors based on their embeddings, introducing substantial structure redundancy. To address this, we propose a novel Informative Graph Structure Learning method (InGSL), which jointly considers both similarity and diversity in edge construction by incorporating a mutual-information-guided learning strategy. Notably, InGSL serves as a plug-in module that can be seamlessly integrated into existing GSL frameworks. Through extensive experiments on six representative GSL methods, we demonstrate that InGSL achieves significant performance improvements at a reduced number of edges.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Informative Graph Structure Learning (InGSL), a novel module that optimizes graph connections by considering both similarity and diversity, guided by mutual information. This addresses the redundancy issue in traditional edge-heavy GSL methods, resulting in denser, more informative graphs with fewer edges.
data_sources: The input data for this method is general graph-structured data, which, in a financial context, could represent relationships between assets, market movers, or time-series dependencies derived from embedding spaces.
alpha_potential: This research enhances the efficiency and effectiveness of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) used for financial modeling. In trading, GNNs are used to model complex inter-asset relationships (e.g., sector contagion, supply chains). By creating a more informative and less redundant connectivity structure (graph), InGSL allows GNN models to capture crucial dependencies more accurately and efficiently, potentially leading to better predictions in portfolio construction, risk management, and factor modeling based on relational data.
title_cn: 信息图结构学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种信息图结构学习（InGSL）方法，通过引入互信息指导的学习策略来平衡相似性和多样性，从而在减少边数量的同时增强图结构的有效性。这可被应用于优化金融图神经网络（GNN）模型，提高资产关系建模的效率和准确性，进而增强基于关系数据的投资组合优化和因子预测策略的性能。

title: NeuroMAS: Multi-Agent Systems as Neural Networks with Joint Reinforcement Learning
summary: Multi-agent language systems are often built as hand-designed workflows, where agents are assigned semantic roles and communication protocols are specified in advance. We propose NeuroMAS, a method that first treats a multi-agent language system as a trainable and scalable neural-network-like architecture with LLM agents as nodes and intermediate textual signals as edges. In NeuroMAS, agent nodes are role-free but structure-aware: the topology only determines how information can flow in general, while reinforcement learning training determines how nodes communicate, specialize, and coordinate. This formulation shifts multi-agent design from workflow engineering toward architecture design, where depth, width, connectivity, and growth protocol become scalable sources of capability. Further, we provide a theoretical perspective showing why such modular textual computation is more parameter-efficient when tasks admit hierarchical decompositions. Experiments show that NeuroMAS improves significantly over both inference-time and trained multi-agent baselines. We further find that organizational scaling is path-dependent: larger systems can be challenging to train from scratch, but become feasible when grown progressively from smaller trained systems. These results suggest that learned neural multi-agent systems are a promising scaling axis for LLMs.
core_methodology: The paper introduces NeuroMAS, a framework that models multi-agent language systems as scalable neural network architectures where LLM agents act as nodes. Communication and specialization emerge through joint reinforcement learning, rather than being hand-designed. This shifts methodology from workflow engineering to architecture design, focusing on connectivity and progressive growth.
data_sources: The primary data source appears to be textual signals used for communication and task execution among agents, likely derived from financial news, reports, or market commentary, although the abstract focuses on the general language system aspect.
alpha_potential: The core potential lies in using NeuroMAS to develop sophisticated, adaptive agents for tasks requiring complex reasoning, coordination, and information synthesis, such as automated news analysis, generating investment theses, or coordinating trading decisions across multiple sub-strategies. The methodology's emphasis on learned coordination and hierarchical decomposition might lead to more efficient processing of unstructured financial data compared to rigid, task-specific pipelines.
title_cn: NeuroMAS：将多智能体系统视为具有联合强化学习的神经网络
summary_cn: NeuroMAS将多智能体语言系统建模为可训练的神经网络架构，利用强化学习使AI代理自主学习通信和专业化。该框架有望应用于金融领域，通过学习更有效的结构和协调机制，提升对非结构化金融数据（如新闻和报告）的复杂分析和决策能力，从而发现潜在的量化Alpha信号。

title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps
summary: We develop a quantitative statistical theory of transformers in the large-context regime by adopting the abstraction of contextual flow maps (CFMs): dynamical systems that evolve a distinguished token in the presence of a contextual measure across a stack of attention blocks. Within this framework, the finite-context model approximates an idealized infinite-context system in which the contextual measure is replaced by its underlying population, so that the context length $n$ becomes a statistical resource. Exploiting the McKean--Vlasov structure of the dynamics and the classical machinery of propagation of chaos, we establish a forward bound controlling the deviation between the finite- and infinite-context CFMs uniformly along depth, and a backward bound controlling the deviation between the corresponding training trajectories uniformly across iterations of online gradient descent. Both bounds achieve the optimal Wasserstein rate $n^{-1/d}$ for general CFMs and parametric rate $n^{-1/2}$ for a restricted class of CFMs that includes transformers as a special case. The analysis rests on a new Eulerian adjoint formulation of the loss gradient and stability estimates for the resulting forward--adjoint system, both of which may be of independent interest.
core_methodology: The paper develops a statistical theory for Transformers in the large-context limit by modeling them as Contextual Flow Maps (CFMs), which are dynamical systems. It uses the machinery of 'propagation of chaos' within the McKean--Vlasov structure to establish theoretical bounds on the deviation between finite-context models and idealized infinite-context systems. This analysis includes bounds on trajectory deviations under online gradient descent.
data_sources: The analysis focuses on the structure and dynamics of the attention mechanism itself, not specific financial datasets. The 'data' context is the input sequence length ($n$) in a Transformer model.
alpha_potential: While the paper is highly theoretical and mathematical, understanding the stability and convergence properties of large-context Transformers (CFMs) under training (online gradient descent) is crucial for developing robust, large-scale financial models. Specifically, the analysis of how context length ($n$) impacts model stability provides a theoretical foundation for optimizing context window sizing in LLMs used for time-series forecasting or complex market regime analysis, potentially leading to more stable or faster-converging trading agents.
title_cn: 上下文流图背景下的混沌传播
summary_cn: 该研究为大上下文限制下的Transformer建立了统计理论，将其抽象为上下文流图（CFM）。它通过混沌传播理论量化了有限上下文模型与理想化无限上下文系统之间的偏差。对于量化交易，此理论为优化在金融时间序列预测中使用的超长上下文Transformer模型的鲁棒性和收敛性提供了深厚的数学基础，有助于构建更稳定、可信赖的AI交易策略。

title: The Score Kalman Filter
summary: A central obstacle in nonlinear Bayesian filtering is representing the belief distribution. Moment-based filters address this by propagating polynomial moments and reconstructing a density from them. Recent work completes the predict-update loop via the maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) principle, but each step requires the partition function and its gradient, both $n$-dimensional integrals whose cost scales exponentially, restricting the demonstrated MaxEnt moment filtering to $n \le 4$. We avoid the partition function entirely by combining score matching with Stein's identity. In our setting, score matching reduces the density fit to a single linear solve whose coefficients are assembled directly from the propagated moments. The same parameters then drive Stein's identity to close the moment hierarchy during prediction and to recover posterior moments after each Bayesian update, keeping the full predict-update loop free of partition function evaluation. The resulting Score Kalman Filter (SKF) reduces to the classical information-form Kalman filter as a special case and performs every step through linear algebra. On nonlinear coupled-oscillator networks, the SKF runs through $n=20$ and reports lower RMSE than the EKF, UKF, EnKF, and particle-filter baselines on the tested synthetic benchmarks.
core_methodology: The Score Kalman Filter (SKF) introduces a novel approach to nonlinear Bayesian filtering by employing score matching and Stein's identity to avoid computing the costly partition function required in Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt) moment filters. This allows the filter to efficiently propagate polynomial moments and perform state estimation via purely linear algebra operations. It scales efficiently to higher dimensions ($n=20$ demonstrated) compared to partition-function-based methods.
data_sources: The paper demonstrates performance on synthetic nonlinear coupled-oscillator networks, simulating dynamic systems. For financial applications, this methodology would be applied to time-series data exhibiting complex, nonlinear dynamics, such as high-frequency market order flow, volatility surfaces, or complex asset price paths.
alpha_potential: The SKF offers a computationally efficient and high-accuracy tool for state estimation in highly nonlinear systems. In quantitative finance, this is crucial for estimating latent factors (e.g., true volatility, underlying latent state in HMMs, or unobserved microstructure parameters) where traditional Kalman filters fail due to nonlinearity. Its superior performance (lower RMSE than EKF, UKF, EnKF, particle filters) on complex benchmarks suggests a significant advantage in modeling complex market regimes, potentially leading to better risk management, more accurate prediction of noisy signals, and improved tracking in dynamic portfolio optimization schemes.
title_cn: 评分卡尔曼滤波器 (Score Kalman Filter)
summary_cn: 评分卡尔曼滤波器（SKF）是一种高效的非线性贝叶斯滤波方法，通过结合分数匹配和Stein恒等式，避免了计算高维积分的配分函数。该方法仅通过线性代数操作完成预测-更新循环，在更高维度（n=20）上表现出优于传统滤波器（如EKF, UKF）的性能。在金融领域，SKF可用于精确估计复杂的、非线性的潜在市场状态或风险因子，尤其适用于高频交易中的微观结构建模和先进的因子投资组合优化，从而提高信号跟踪精度和风险预测能力。

title: SCOUT: Cyclic Causal Discovery Under Soft Interventions with Unknown Targets
summary: Learning causal relationships between variables from data is a fundamental research area with many applications across disciplines. Most existing causal discovery algorithms rely on the assumptions that (i) the underlying system is acyclic, (ii) the exogenous noise variables are Gaussian, and (iii) the intervention targets for the data-generating experiments are known. While these assumptions simplify the analysis, they are violated in real-life systems. Most existing methods that address these issues either assume the underlying model is linear or are constrained to operate in limited interventional settings. To that end, we propose SCOUT, a novel causal discovery framework for learning nonlinear cyclic causal relationships from soft interventional data with unknown targets. Our approach maximizes the data log-likelihood to recover the graph structure, using two normalizing-flow architectures: contractive residual flows and neural spline flows. Through experiments on synthetic and real-world data, we show that SCOUT outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both causal graph recovery and unknown target recovery across various interventional and noise settings.
core_methodology: SCOUT is a novel causal discovery framework designed to learn nonlinear, cyclic causal relationships from observational data incorporating soft interventions where the intervention targets are unknown. It leverages two normalizing-flow architectures—contractive residual flows and neural spline flows—to maximize the data log-likelihood for recovering the underlying causal graph structure.
data_sources: This method is designed for time-series data that includes soft interventional experiments. In finance, this could be applied to high-frequency market data, macroeconomic indicators, or experimental trading environments where specific exogenous shocks or policy changes (interventions) are introduced, even if the exact timing or scale of the intervention is stochastic ('soft').
alpha_potential: The ability to accurately model complex, cyclic, and nonlinear causal links in financial systems is crucial for building robust trading strategies. Traditional models often struggle with feedback loops inherent in markets (e.g., price discovery, liquidity effects). SCOUT's strength lies in identifying these cyclic relationships and handling non-Gaussian noise. This can lead to more stable factor models, better risk attribution, and potentially identifying leads/lags in complex macroeconomic or cross-asset relationships, providing an edge in forecasting and portfolio construction.
title_cn: SCOUT：软干预下具有未知目标的循环因果发现
summary_cn: SCOUT提出了一种学习非线性循环因果关系的新框架，特别适用于含有软干预且干预目标未知的数据。该方法结合了残差流和神经样条流架构，可用于发现金融时间序列中复杂的反馈循环和潜在驱动因素。这有助于构建更鲁棒的风险模型、优化因子结构或识别资产间的深层因果依赖，从而提高预测准确性和策略稳定性。

title: Tensor Cookbook: Mastering Tensors through Diagrams
summary: High-dimensional data arise naturally in many areas of science and engineering, including machine learning, signal processing, computational physics, and statistics. Such data are often represented as tensors, multi-dimensional generalizations of matrices. While tensors provide a natural representation for multi-modal structure, their direct manipulation quickly becomes challenging as the order grows: the number of parameters increases exponentially, and algebraic expressions involving many indices become difficult to interpret and implement. Tensor networks (TNs) provide an effective framework for addressing these challenges. Originally introduced by Penrose and developed extensively in quantum physics, the graphical language of tensor networks encodes contractions as edges in a graph, reducing notational overhead and revealing structural properties obscured by index notation. Despite the central role of high-dimensional tensors in modern machine learning and numerical analysis, tensor network diagrams remain underutilized outside quantum computing, partly due to the lack of a self-contained mathematical reference accessible to a broad technical audience. This manuscript provides a self-contained guide to tensor networks and their use in tensor algebra. We present the main operations on tensors, contractions, products, and reshaping through, graphical notation, and show how classical tensor decompositions and related computations are naturally expressed in this framework. We also illustrate how tensor networks simplify the derivation of gradients and the manipulation of high-dimensional probability distributions. Throughout, we show that the diagrammatic approach yields genuinely shorter and more transparent proofs of classical identities, rank bounds, and gradient formulas that would otherwise require laborious index manipulation.
core_methodology: This paper focuses on Tensor Networks (TNs) and their diagrammatic representation for handling high-dimensional algebraic operations, particularly tensor contractions. It provides a framework to simplify complex tensor algebra, making calculations involving high-order tensors more efficient and interpretable. The core technique is using graphical notation to manage tensor decompositions, reshaping, and gradient calculations.
data_sources: The methodology is general and not tied to specific financial data. It applies to any high-dimensional data representations, such as feature vectors in deep learning models, high-dimensional covariance matrices, or complex time-series representations.
alpha_potential: While the paper does not present a strategy, the methodology is highly relevant for enhancing existing AI/ML trading models. Deep learning models often rely on high-dimensional tensors (e.g., in Transformer architectures or complex feature engineering). Tensor Networks can facilitate more efficient training, inference, and parameter reduction (compression) of these models, particularly beneficial for training high-capacity models on large financial datasets where computational efficiency is critical.
title_cn: 张量食谱：通过图解掌握张量操作
summary_cn: 该论文介绍了张量网络（TN）及其图解法，用于高效处理高维张量代数。其价值在于能简化复杂高维数据（如深度学习模型中的张量）的运算和梯度计算，有助于优化金融领域的复杂机器学习模型（如Transformer或GNN），提高训练和推理效率。

title: Automatic Unsupervised Ensemble Outlier Model Selection--Extended Version
summary: Unsupervised outlier detection is attractive because it eliminates the need for labeled data. Moreover, forming multi-model ensembles can improve detection robustness. However, composing an ensemble without labeled data is challenging. Naively composed ensembles can suffer from ensemble saturation, where redundant or unreliable detection models degrade performance and incur unnecessary computation. We propose MetaEns, an automatic unsupervised framework for selecting ensembles of outlier detection models. Using labeled meta-datasets, MetaEns learns a model that predicts marginal ensemble gains, estimating the expected improvement from adding a candidate model to a partially constructed ensemble. At test time, this learned signal is combined with a submodular-inspired proxy objective that enforces diminishing returns through diversity-aware discounting and family-level risk regularization, thereby enabling greedy sequential selection with adaptive early stopping. As a result, MetaEns constructs compact, high-quality ensembles without access to ground-truth labels. Experiments on 39 real-world datasets show that MetaEns consistently outperforms state-of-the-art unsupervised selectors and ensemble baselines, achieving higher average precision while using fewer models.
core_methodology: The paper proposes MetaEns, an unsupervised framework for building robust ensembles of outlier detection models. It uses labeled meta-datasets to learn a model that predicts the marginal gain of adding a new model to an ensemble. This learned signal is combined with a diversification-aware objective (submodular-inspired proxy) to guide greedy sequential selection, ensuring a high-quality, compact ensemble without needing ground-truth labels at the final selection time.
data_sources: The paper uses 39 real-world datasets for validation, though the specific domain of these datasets is not detailed, the methodology implies applicability to any time-series or cross-sectional data where anomaly detection is needed.
alpha_potential: Outlier detection is crucial in quantitative finance for identifying rare events, potential market manipulation, data corruption, or rare market regime shifts. A robust, unsupervised ensemble method like MetaEns could be used to define dynamic thresholds for volatility spikes, unusual trade volumes, or anomalous correlations between assets. This directly supports risk management, regime switching models, and potentially identifying precursors to extreme price movements (alpha signal generation or risk mitigation).
title_cn: 自动无监督集成离群点模型选择——扩展版
summary_cn: 该研究提出MetaEns框架，用于自动构建鲁棒的无监督离群点检测模型集成。该方法通过学习预测集成增益的方式，在无需标签的情况下，智能选择最佳模型组合，拒绝冗余模型。在金融领域，这可用于实时识别市场中的异常交易、极端波动事件或数据质量问题，从而提升风险控制和市场微观结构分析的准确性，支持更可靠的策略决策。

title: Global Convergence of Sampling-Based Nonconvex Optimization through Diffusion-Style Smoothing
summary: Sampling-based optimization (SBO), like cross-entropy method and evolutionary algorithms, has achieved many successes in solving non-convex problems without gradients, yet its convergence is poorly understood. In this paper, we establish a non-asymptotic convergence analysis for SBO through the lens of smoothing. Specifically, we recast SBO as gradient descent on a smoothed objective, mirroring noise-conditioned score ascent in diffusion models. Our first contribution is a landscape analysis of the smoothed objective, demonstrating how smoothing helps escape local minima and uncovering a fundamental coverage-optimality trade-off: smoothing renders the landscape more benign by enlarging the locally convex region around the global minimizer, but at the cost of introducing an optimality gap. Building on this insight, we establish non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for SBO algorithms to a neighborhood of the global minimizer. Furthermore, we propose an annealed SBO algorithm, Diffusion-Inspired Dual-Annealing (DIDA), which is provably convergent to the global optimum. We conduct extensive numerical experiments to verify our landscape results and also demonstrate the compelling performance of DIDA compared to other gradient-free optimization methods. Lastly, we discuss implications of our results for diffusion models.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes Sampling-Based Optimization (SBO) methods (like genetic algorithms or particle swarm optimization) by reframing them as gradient descent on a smoothed objective function, analogous to diffusion models. It establishes theoretical convergence guarantees and proposes a new annealed SBO algorithm, DIDA, which provably converges to the global optimum for non-convex problems.
data_sources: The methodology is applicable to any optimization problem where gradient information is unavailable or undesirable. In quantitative finance, this applies directly to high-dimensional, non-convex tasks such as portfolio optimization (e.g., maximizing Sharpe ratio with complex constraints), parameter tuning for trading models, or hyperparameter optimization for deep learning models in finance.
alpha_potential: The core value is the robust, convergence-guaranteed optimization method for solving intractable non-convex problems relevant to finance. Strategies such as complex, high-dimensional portfolio construction, model calibration where the objective function is rough (e.g., certain risk parity or factor timing models), or finding global optima in reinforcement learning environments can benefit significantly from guaranteed convergence provided by DIDA, potentially leading to superior portfolio allocations or more robust model parameters.
title_cn: 采样基优化在扩散式平滑中的非凸优化的全局收敛性
summary_cn: 该研究提供了一种新的、具有理论收敛保证的无梯度优化算法（DIDA）。该方法适用于处理量化金融中常见的复杂、高维、非凸优化问题，例如具有复杂约束条件的投资组合构建或深度学习模型的鲁棒参数调优。其优势在于能有效收敛到全局最优解，为策略设计和模型校准提供了更可靠的工具。

title: Mechanism Learning: Prototype-Anchored Mechanism Inference for Scientific Forecasting
summary: Scientific forecasting typically relies on direct state prediction, an approach that grows brittle under data scarcity, extended horizons, non-stationary dynamics, or high-dimensional complexity. While raw state trajectories are highly sensitive in these regimes, underlying local evolution rules often exhibit robust reusability. We introduce mechanism learning, a framework that forecasts future states by estimating the currently active local mechanism. Our method compresses local spatiotemporal fragments into mechanism descriptors, forming a data-driven, structured mechanism space where proximity reflects similar local evolution rules. To ground these estimates in observed data, we utilize prototype anchors, a set of representative mechanisms that sparsely cover the space of local rules. We evaluate this approach on Burgers dynamics, WeatherBench2, and Lorenz96. Empirically, the learned mechanism spaces resist collapse and maintain strong local consistency. Compared to direct prediction and other models including FNO, NODE, LSTM, and reservoir-family methods, our framework demonstrates predictive gains in fragile regimes: it significantly improves switching stability in Burgers dynamics and achieves state-of-the-art performance both under the scarce-data fixed-horizon WeatherBench2 protocol and in intermediate-complexity Lorenz96. Ablation studies and drift diagnostics confirm that these improvements are driven by finite prototype anchoring rather than sheer latent capacity. Together, these results establish mechanism learning as a principled, robust alternative to direct state prediction in forecasting complex systems.
core_methodology: The framework introduces 'mechanism learning,' which forecasts future states by estimating the active local evolution mechanism rather than direct state prediction. It compresses local spatiotemporal fragments into mechanism descriptors, creating a structured space where proximity signifies similar evolution rules. Crucially, it uses 'prototype anchors' (representative mechanisms) to ground the estimates effectively, especially under data scarcity or non-stationary conditions.
data_sources: The paper focuses on complex physical and environmental dynamics (Burgers dynamics, WeatherBench2, Lorenz96). For quantitative finance application, this implies a need to map raw financial time series, microstructure data, or high-frequency order book data as the 'spatiotemporal fragments' to analyze underlying market regimes or microstructure rules.
alpha_potential: The core strength lies in robust forecasting under non-stationary and data-scarce regimes. In finance, markets are highly non-stationary and exhibit regime shifts (e.g., volatility clustering, structural breaks). If the 'local evolution rules' (mechanisms) can be learned from high-frequency order flow or short historical market patches, this method offers a theoretically robust way to predict the short-term continuation or switching behavior of market dynamics beyond standard stationary assumptions or simple direct prediction (like standard LSTMs/Transformers). This is highly relevant for regime-aware trading or microstructure strategies.
title_cn: 机制学习：面向科学预测的原型锚定机制推断
summary_cn: 该方法通过学习和推断“局部演化机制”而非直接预测状态，提高了复杂系统（如金融市场）在数据稀疏或非平稳条件下的预测鲁棒性。其核心价值在于对抗市场结构突变和高频噪声，有望用于建立更稳定的市场微观结构预测模型或高频信号的机制驱动交易策略。

title: ACIL: Auto Chain of Thoughts for In-Context Learning
summary: Recent advances in large language models (LLMs) have shown that Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning can substantially improve performance on complex reasoning tasks. At the same time, In-Context Learning (ICL) has become an important mechanism for adapting LLMs to new tasks without updating model parameters, using only examples provided in the prompt. However, standard ICL often struggles on tasks that require multi-step reasoning, because the demonstrations usually contain only input-output pairs and lack explicit intermediate reasoning steps. This paper introduces an Automatic Chain-of-Thought (Auto-CoT) framework to improve ICL by automatically constructing reasoning-enhanced demonstrations. Auto-CoT generates reasoning chains for input-output examples, augments the prompt context with structured intermediate explanations, and removes irrelevant or low-quality demonstrations through a systematic selection process. By incorporating high-quality reasoning examples into the ICL prompt, Auto-CoT guides the model toward more reliable reasoning and improves prediction accuracy. Experiments across multiple reasoning tasks demonstrate that the proposed framework improves ICL performance by providing explicit intermediate reasoning guidance.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Auto-CoT, a framework to automatically generate Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning steps for In-Context Learning (ICL) demonstrations. This method enriches prompts with structured intermediate explanations and employs a selection process to filter lower-quality examples, thereby guiding LLMs toward more robust reasoning in few-shot learning contexts.
data_sources: The primary data sources are typical benchmark datasets used for testing LLM reasoning capabilities (e.g., mathematical, logical reasoning tasks). In a financial context, these would be adapted to structured financial tasks requiring multi-step logic (e.g., complex earnings call analysis, deriving trading rules from regulatory documents).
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on general reasoning tasks, the Auto-CoT methodology has significant potential for complex financial applications where multi-step reasoning is crucial. This includes interpreting dense financial reports, synthesizing information across various unstructured data sources (news, transcripts, regulations) to form a coherent investment thesis, or automating the derivation of complex factor interactions. By improving LLM's reasoning fidelity in few-shot setups, it could lead to more reliable quantitative signals extracted from qualitative data.
title_cn: ACIL：用于上下文学习的自动思维链
summary_cn: 该方法通过自动生成高质量的思维链（CoT）推理示例，显著增强大型语言模型（LLM）在少样本学习（ICL）中的推理能力。在金融领域，这可用于改进LLM对复杂财报、监管文件多步骤的逻辑分析，从而提高非结构化数据的信息提取和决策支持效率。

title: Reliability and Effectiveness of Autonomous AI Agents in Supply Chain Management
summary: This paper studies autonomous generative AI agents in multi-echelon supply chains using the MIT Beer Game. We identify four inference-time levers that shape performance: model selection, policies and guardrails, centralized data sharing, and prompt engineering. Model capability is the dominant factor: an out-of-the-box reasoning model exceeds human-level performance, and optimized reasoning models reduce costs by up to 67% relative to human teams. However, strong average performance masks substantial reliability risks. We introduce the agent bullwhip effect, the amplification of decision unreliability across echelons, manifesting along two dimensions: decision variance increases both across facilities at the same point in time and within the same facility across time. We develop a mathematical framework showing that this phenomenon is inherent to multi-agent systems that involve coordination and information delays, and we demonstrate that repeated sampling fails to meaningfully reduce it. To address this limitation, we propose a Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO)-based reinforcement-learning post-training framework that trains a shared base LLM using system-level supply-chain rewards. GRPO post-training substantially reduces tail events, curtails agent bullwhip, and improves the reliability of autonomous supply-chain agents.
core_methodology: The research focuses on using autonomous generative AI agents (LLMs) within multi-echelon supply chain simulations (MIT Beer Game). It employs inference-time levers (model selection, guardrails, context sharing, prompt engineering) and proposes a specialized Reinforcement Learning post-training framework, Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO), using system-level rewards to enhance agent reliability and reduce the 'agent bullwhip effect.'
data_sources: Simulated supply chain data based on the structure and dynamics of the MIT Beer Game, focusing on inventory, orders, and demand signals across networked agents.
alpha_potential: While the paper directly addresses supply chain management, the core contribution lies in addressing the reliability and instability (bullwhip effect) of multi-agent LLM systems under coordination and information delay. These concepts are highly transferable to financial markets, specifically in modeling systemic risk, coordination failures in high-frequency trading networks, or multi-agent portfolio management where agents must coordinate trades or interact based on delayed information. The GRPO post-training framework for stabilizing decentralized AI systems could be adapted to create robust trading agents.
title_cn: 自主人工智能体在供应链管理中的可靠性与有效性研究
summary_cn: 该研究使用生成式AI智能体解决供应链中的协调问题。其提出的GRPO强化学习后训练框架，旨在通过系统级奖励优化，显著降低多智能体系统中的决策方差（“代理牛鞭效应”）。该方法对于构建在信息延迟和系统协调下更稳定、更可靠的量化交易智能体模型具有借鉴价值。

title: CAST: Causal Anchored Simplex Transport for Distribution-Valued Time Series
summary: Many decision-facing stochastic systems are observed through aggregate distributions rather than scalar trajectories: queue occupancies, mobility shares, public-health mixtures, generation-source shares, ecological compositions, and air-quality severity profiles all live on the probability simplex and evolve over time. We study causal (online) forecasting for these distribution-valued time series and argue that the transition operator itself should be structured around the simplex. We introduce CAST (Causal Anchored Simplex Transport), a successor-local operator that (i) retrieves empirical successors from causal context, (ii) stabilizes them with a persistence anchor, and (iii) applies a bounded local stochastic transport on ordered supports; every stage preserves the simplex by construction. We identify a structural failure mode, latent transition-kernel aliasing, where similar observed distributions evolve differently under different contextual regimes, and prove that any forecaster depending only on an aliased summary incurs an irreducible weighted Jensen-Shannon excess-risk lower bound, while the CAST hypothesis class contains the regime-aware Bayes successor; for ordered supports an additional Pinsker separation holds whenever the transported successor lies outside the no-transport anchor hull. On eleven public and simulated benchmarks spanning ecology, energy, diet, mortality, employment, air quality, severe weather, mobility, and G/G/1, G_t/G/1 queue occupancy, CAST attains the best average rank on both one-step KL (1.27) and autoregressive rollout JSD (1.91), winning 8/11 sections on each metric against a broad statistical, compositional, recurrent, convolutional, and Transformer baseline set, and top-2 on all 11 sections for offline KL. Component ablations and a controlled synthetic aliasing experiment corroborate the theory.
core_methodology: CAST (Causal Anchored Simplex Transport) is a novel forecasting operator designed specifically for time series whose values reside on the probability simplex (i.e., they are distributions). It is a local operator that handles causal inference by retrieving empirical successors, stabilizing them with a persistence anchor, and applying bounded local stochastic transport, ensuring the output remains a valid distribution. It explicitly addresses the failure mode of 'latent transition-kernel aliasing.'
data_sources: The paper tested the method on diverse distribution-valued time series including energy generation source shares, mobility shares, mortality, employment, and various queueing time series, demonstrating its generality. While not directly using financial market data in the reported benchmarks, the methodology is applicable to financial data represented as distributions.
alpha_potential: The approach is highly relevant for forecasting financial quantities that naturally manifest as distributions, such as cross-sectional asset allocation weights, market-implied volatility surfaces, sector/factor exposure distributions, or order book pressure profiles. By explicitly modeling transitions on the simplex and handling distributional aliasing, CAST could potentially generate more stable and accurate forecasts for these complex, compositionally constrained variables compared to standard non-compositional time series models (like vanilla RNNs or Transformers). This improved forecasting capability for portfolio constraints or risk measures could form the basis for better portfolio optimization or risk parity strategies.
title_cn: CAST：用于值域为分布的时间序列的因果锚定单形传输
summary_cn: CAST方法专为预测驻留在概率单形上的时间序列（如资产配置权重、市场情绪分布）。它通过结构化算子确保预测结果保持为有效分布，并解决了复杂上下文下的信号混叠问题。在金融领域，这可用于更精确地预测和优化受约束的组合成分或风险分布，从而提升基于分布预测的量化策略表现。

title: Reasoning Can Be Restored by Correcting a Few Decision Tokens
summary: Large reasoning models (LRMs) substantially outperform their base LLM counterparts on challenging reasoning benchmarks, yet it remains poorly understood where base models go wrong during token-by-token generation and how to narrow this gap efficiently. We study the base-reasoning gap through quantifying token-level distributional disagreement between a base model and a stronger reasoning model using likelihood-based divergences. Across benchmarks, we find that the reasoning advantage is highly sparse and concentrates on a small set of early, planning-related decision tokens. For instance, on Qwen3-0.6B, only ~8% of generated tokens account for the salient disagreement, and these tokens concentrate early in the response, are strongly enriched in planning-related decisions (17x), and coincide with high base-model uncertainty -- suggesting that base models fail mainly at early planning points that steer the subsequent reasoning trajectory. Building on these findings, we propose disagreement-guided token intervention, a simple inference-time delegation scheme that performs a one-token takeover by the reasoning model only at high-disagreement positions and immediately switches back to the base model. With a small intervention budget, this sparse delegation substantially recovers and can even surpass the performance of a same-size reasoning model on challenging reasoning tasks. Code is available at https://github.com/AlphaLab-USTC/RRTokenIntervention.
core_methodology: The paper proposes Disagreement-Guided Token Intervention, an inference-time delegation scheme. It identifies 'disagreement' between a base LLM and a stronger reasoning model at critical decision points (planning tokens) and selectively overrides the base model's output at these high-disagreement points, effectively correcting sparse, early planning errors. This technique improves performance with minimal intervention cost.
data_sources: The study uses general reasoning benchmarks (e.g., GSM8K, MATH, BigBench-Hard) to analyze LLM failure modes. While not using financial data directly, the methodology concerns improving core reasoning capabilities of foundation models.
alpha_potential: This research does not describe a direct trading strategy, but it significantly improves the reliability and performance of foundational LLMs. For quantitative finance, this is highly relevant for tasks requiring complex chain-of-thought reasoning, such as interpreting unstructured financial news, generating complex legal/regulatory compliance assessments, or refining multi-step trading agent logic. By making reasoning models 'more correct' with fewer errors, it paves the way for more robust AI agents in decision-making pipelines within a quant framework.
title_cn: 推理可以通过修正少数决策Token来恢复
summary_cn: 该研究提出一种推理时的方法，通过识别基础模型与高级推理模型之间的关键决策Token分歧，并仅在这些关键点进行干预，有效地修正推理错误。虽然不直接涉及金融数据，但该技术能显著提高复杂金融推理任务中LLM代理的可靠性和准确性，适用于新闻解读和复杂策略生成等应用。

title: MixSD: Mixed Contextual Self-Distillation for Knowledge Injection
summary: Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) is widely used to inject new knowledge into language models, but it often degrades pretrained capabilities such as reasoning and general-domain performance. We argue this forgetting arises because fine-tuning targets from humans or external systems diverge from the model's autoregressive distribution, forcing the optimizer to imitate low-probability token sequences. To address this problem, we propose MixSD, a simple external-teacher-free method for distribution-aligned knowledge injection. Instead of training on fixed targets, MixSD constructs supervision dynamically by mixing tokens from two conditionals of the base model itself: an expert conditional that observes the injected fact in context, and a naive conditional that reflects the model's original prior. The resulting supervision sequences preserve the factual learning signal while remaining substantially closer to the base model's distribution. We evaluate MixSD on two synthetic corpora that we construct to study factual recall and arithmetic function acquisition in a controlled setting, together with established benchmarks for open-domain factual question answering and knowledge editing. Across multiple model scales and settings, MixSD consistently achieves a better memorization-retention trade-off compared to SFT and on-policy self distillation baselines, retaining up to 100% of the base model's held-out capability while maintaining near-perfect training accuracy, whereas standard SFT retains as little as 1%. We further show that MixSD produces substantially lower-NLL supervision targets under the base model and reduces harmful movement along Fisher-sensitive parameter directions. These results suggest that aligning supervision with the model's native generation distribution is a simple and effective principle for knowledge injection that mitigates catastrophic forgetting.
core_methodology: MixSD is a novel knowledge injection technique for Language Models (LLMs) that mitigates catastrophic forgetting (degradation of pretrained capabilities) during Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT). It achieves this by dynamically constructing supervision targets that mix tokens from the model's 'expert' conditional (observing the new fact) and its 'naive' conditional (reflecting the original prior distribution). This aligns the fine-tuning process more closely with the model's native generation distribution.
data_sources: The paper primarily uses synthetic corpora for controlled experiments on factual recall and arithmetic, and established benchmarks for open-domain QA and knowledge editing. For finance, this implies the methodology applies to updating models trained on general financial corpora or proprietary data.
alpha_potential: While MixSD itself is not a trading strategy, it is a crucial methodology advancement for effectively updating LLMs used in quantitative finance. High-frequency trading systems, market regime detection, and alternative data analysis often rely on LLMs trained on evolving information. The ability to inject new market knowledge (e.g., regulatory changes, reaction to CPI reports) without sacrificing general reasoning/analytical capabilities (avoiding catastrophic forgetting) makes LLMs more reliable and robust for downstream alpha generation tasks. This improves the stability and efficacy of any AI/ML-driven strategy relying on LLMs for research or execution.
title_cn: MixSD：用于知识注入的混合情境自蒸馏
summary_cn: MixSD提供了一种有效的LLM知识注入方法，解决了微调中旧能力丧失的问题。这对于量化交易至关重要，因为它允许金融机构在不损害模型通用推理能力的前提下，安全地更新LLM以吸收最新的市场数据、法规变化或特定领域的专业知识。这能提高依赖LLM进行数据分析和信号提取的交易系统的稳健性。

title: Plan First, Diffuse Later: Extrinsic Graph Guidance for Long-Horizon Diffusion Planning
summary: Compositional diffusion models offer a promising route to long-horizon planning by denoising multiple overlapping sub-trajectories while ensuring that together they constitute a global solution. However, enforcing local behavior over long chains is often insufficient for a coherent global structure to emerge. Recent works tackle this limitation through intrinsic search, which explores multiple paths during the denoising process. While intrinsic search improves global coherence, it comes at the cost of repeated evaluations of an already compute-heavy model. In this work, we argue that extrinsic search, performed outside the denoising process, offers a more effective mode of exploration for long-horizon planning while naturally enabling the use of classical algorithms to solve unseen combinatorial tasks at test time. Our eXtrinsic search-guided Diffuser (XDiffuser) first computes a plan over a state-space graph -- serving as a lightweight local connectivity oracle for the diffusion model. The plan is then used to guide denoising for a single trajectory, effectively offloading the burden of exploration. XDiffuser outperforms diffusion-based baselines on long-horizon tasks, with particularly large gains in the low-quality data regime and on unseen tasks beyond goal-reaching, including multi-agent coordination and TSP-style reasoning. Project website: https://yanivhass.github.io/XDiffuser-site/
core_methodology: The paper introduces XDiffuser, a method combining extrinsic graph-based planning with diffusion models for long-horizon planning. It uses a pre-computed state-space graph plan (extrinsic search) to guide the denoising process (intrinsic diffusion) for a single trajectory, aiming for global coherence without excessive internal exploration. This structure offloads exploration complexity to the planner.
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on planning tasks like multi-agent coordination and the Traveling Salesperson Problem (TSP) style reasoning, which are generally abstract combinatorial optimization problems, rather than direct financial market data.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on general planning and robotics, the core idea—decoupling high-level structured planning (the 'plan first' graph search) from low-level trajectory generation (the 'diffuse later' diffusion model)—has significant potential for complex financial sequencing problems. This could apply to multi-step optimization in portfolio construction, sequence optimization for high-frequency trading maneuvers, or coordinating multiple interacting trading agents. Its performance in 'unseen' combinatorial tasks suggests robust adaptability, which is valuable for dynamic market regimes.
title_cn: 先规划后扩散：用于长程扩散规划的外在图引导
summary_cn: 该研究提出XDiffuser框架，它将外在的图搜索规划（作为局部连通性预设）与扩散模型采样相结合，有效解决了长程规划的全局协调性问题。此方法论可借鉴于复杂的金融序列建模，如多资产投资组合的构建序列、高频交易中的复杂操作路径优化，或协调多个交易智能体，以实现计算效率高且全局一致的长期策略。

title: Learning to Learn from Multimodal Experience
summary: Experience-driven learning has emerged as a promising paradigm for enabling agents to improve from interaction trajectories by accumulating and reusing past experience. However, existing approaches are predominantly developed in textual settings and rely on manually designed memory schemas, limiting their applicability to multimodal environments. In real-world scenarios, experience is inherently multimodal, involving heterogeneous signals across perception, reasoning, and action, which makes effective memory design significantly more challenging. In particular, the optimal way to structure and utilize multimodal experience is highly task-dependent and evolves over time, rendering fixed memory designs insufficient. In this work, we propose a new paradigm, learning to learn from multimodal experience, which shifts memory design from a predefined component to an adaptive and learnable process. Our framework enables agents to dynamically construct, organize, and utilize memory based on task requirements and interaction history, effectively learning how to structure experience for improved performance. Experiments demonstrate that adaptive memory design substantially enhances agent performance and generalization across multimodal tasks, highlighting the critical role of learning memory mechanisms in experience-driven learning.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a 'learning to learn' paradigm for agents operating in multimodal environments. Instead of relying on fixed memory structures, the framework enables agents to dynamically construct, organize, and utilize memory based on the specific task requirements and interaction history. This adaptive memory design allows the agent to learn the optimal way to structure and retrieve relevant past experiences, which is crucial when dealing with heterogeneous data streams.
data_sources: While the abstract focuses on general multimodal tasks, the implication is the integration of heterogeneous data sources inherent in financial markets, such as price time series (numerical), news/sentiment (textual), order book dynamics (structured sequence), and potentially alternative data streams. The key is managing the *combination* of these modalities.
alpha_potential: The ability to adaptively manage and retrieve experience from multimodal data directly addresses a core challenge in advanced quantitative trading: integrating diverse information sources (e.g., fundamental data, market microstructure, news sentiment) effectively. A trading agent utilizing this framework could learn highly adaptive decision-making policies. For instance, it could learn when to prioritize sentiment patterns over short-term price memory during earnings events, or when to shift focus from historical volatility to real-time order flow memory based on current market states. This leads to more robust and context-aware trading signals than agents using fixed memory structures.
title_cn: 从多模态经验中学习如何学习
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种'学习如何学习'的范式，使智能体能够动态构建和利用记忆，以适应多模态环境下的任务需求。在量化交易中，这意味着更有效地整合价格、新闻、微观结构等异构数据。该框架能让交易代理学会如何组织和检索过去的经验，从而在不同市场状态下生成更具鲁棒性和上下文感知的交易决策，提升策略的泛化能力。

title: Prediction-Intervention Games and Invariant Sets
summary: We consider the following two-player game: using observational data, the leader chooses a prediction function for a response variable $Y$ from given covariates. The follower then reacts with an intervention on some covariates in the underlying structural causal model to maximize their own objective. The leader knows the intervention targets, but may have limited knowledge of the follower's objective. We call this setup a prediction-intervention game, a special case of a Stackelberg game. Finding an optimal strategy for the leader is generally difficult. To avoid severe performance loss, the leader may base their prediction on the causal parents of $Y$, or more generally on an invariant subset of covariates. We prove, for two common classes of follower objectives, that predictors based on the stable blanket, a specific invariant subset, are always better or as good as those based on the causal parents. We further upper bound the leader's post-intervention risk by a worst-case risk over allowed interventions and strengthen existing distribution generalization results to analyze this bound: we give sufficient conditions under which stable-blanket predictors are worst-case optimal, and show by examples that these conditions cannot in general be dropped. Finally, we discuss practical strategies for settings with known and unknown graph, and test them on simulated and real-world data.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the 'prediction-intervention game,' a Stackelberg-like game where a leader makes predictions, and a follower intervenes based on those predictions to maximize their objective. The core technical focus is on using 'invariant sets,' specifically the 'stable blanket,' to devise robust prediction strategies for the leader that minimize performance loss under worst-case follower interventions. This utilizes causal inference concepts to ensure out-of-distribution generalization.
data_sources: The paper focuses on theoretical frameworks tested on simulated data and tested on unspecified real-world data. In a finance context, this methodology would require observational financial time-series data, potentially involving proprietary trading data or tick data where predictor (leader) and reaction dynamics (follower) can be modeled.
alpha_potential: The potential lies in building robust trading models that anticipate and counteract adversarial market reactions or structural shifts ('interventions'). In quantitative finance, this relates to developing 'invariant risk factors' or 'stable predictor variables' for noisy, non-stationary financial data. By selecting predictors from the stable blanket (causal parents plus necessary nodes to ensure invariance), the leader can create strategies resilient to 'concept drift' or structural breaks caused by competitive market participants (the follower). This is highly relevant for long-term factor stability.
title_cn: 预测-干预博弈与不变集
summary_cn: 该研究提出了预测-干预博弈框架，核心在于利用“稳定包络”等不变子集来构建对市场参与者（跟随者）干预具有鲁棒性的预测模型。这为量化交易提供了构建抗结构性变化和对冲交易对手风险的稳健预测信号的方法，有助于开发更具泛化性的因子策略。

title: Learning Unbiased Permutations via Flow Matching
summary: Learning permutations is fundamental to sorting, ranking, and matching, but existing differentiable methods based on entropy-regularized Sinkhorn produce a single softened solution and collapse under ambiguity. We present PermFlow, a conditional flow matching framework that operates directly on the affine subspace of matrices with unit row and column sums. A closed-form tangent-space projector preserves these constraints exactly along every trajectory, by construction rather than through iterative correction, and a nearest-target coupling routes distinct noisy initializations toward distinct valid permutations. The result is a model that captures multimodal permutation distributions rather than collapsing them to a single mode. On a visual sorting task with blended-digit ambiguity and a symmetric linear assignment problem, PermFlow achieves high accuracy on unambiguous inputs and recovers both valid permutations under ambiguity, where Sinkhorn-based baselines structurally fail.
core_methodology: The paper introduces PermFlow, a conditional flow matching framework designed to learn unbiased and multimodal permutation distributions. It operates within the affine subspace of matrices with unit row and column sums, using a closed-form tangent-space projector to maintain constraints exactly, avoiding the mode collapse issues seen in Sinkhorn-based methods when dealing with ambiguous assignments.
data_sources: The paper focuses on theoretical demonstrations using visual sorting tasks and symmetric linear assignment problems, which are artificial datasets. However, the underlying mathematical framework is applicable to any assignment problem involving discrete structures.
alpha_potential: The core value lies in solving accurate assignment problems, particularly when inherent ambiguity exists in the mapping between inputs (e.g., time series or assets). In finance, this is relevant for tasks like optimal asset matching, robust portfolio construction where multiple valid allocations exist but need to be robustly sampled, or dynamic routing/scheduling in high-frequency trading environments where exact assignment under uncertainty is critical. The ability to capture multimodal distributions rather than a single mode is crucial for risk management and generating diverse trading strategies.
title_cn: 通过流匹配学习无偏置的排列
summary_cn: 该研究提出PermFlow框架，用于精确学习具有多模态特性的排列，解决了传统方法在处理模糊分配问题时的模式崩溃。在量化交易中，此技术可用于投资组合优化、资产配对或市场微观结构中的鲁棒分配任务，尤其在存在多个有效映射时，能更准确地捕捉潜在的决策空间。

title: EfficientTDMPC: Improved MPC Objectives for Sample-Efficient Continuous Control
summary: We introduce EfficientTDMPC, a sample-efficient model-based reinforcement learning method for continuous control built on the TD-MPC family of algorithms. Central to this family is a planner that aims to find an action sequence that maximizes the estimated return. The return is estimated using a learned model and value networks, each of which can introduce error. EfficientTDMPC proposes to reduce this error in two ways. First, it introduces an ensemble of dynamics models and averages the return estimates across those models and across different rollout depths. Second, it adds the option to apply an uncertainty penalty to the planner objective, yielding a planner that avoids actions with uncertain return estimates. It then adds practical improvements which increase buffer data freshness and reduce compute. Lastly, we find that our contributions enable EfficientTDMPC to benefit more from a higher update-to-data (UTD) ratio, further improving sample efficiency. To the best of our knowledge, in the low data regime of each benchmark, EfficientTDMPC achieves state-of-the-art (SOTA) in terms of sample efficiency on HumanoidBench-Hard and DMC hard, while matching SOTA on DMC easy.
core_methodology: The paper introduces EfficientTDMPC, a sample-efficient reinforcement learning (RL) algorithm built on TD-MPC. It improves upon existing methods by using an ensemble of dynamics models for averaged return estimation, incorporating an uncertainty penalty into the planner's objective function, and enhancing data freshness. These changes aim to reduce model error and improve reliability in continuous control tasks.
data_sources: The research uses standard continuous control benchmarks (HumanoidBench-Hard, DMC hard/easy), which serve as proxies for complex sequential decision-making problems.
alpha_potential: While the immediate application is in robotics/control simulation, the core innovations—sample-efficient model-based RL, uncertainty-aware planning (using penalties), and ensemble modeling for robustness—are highly relevant for developing complex algorithmic trading agents. A trading agent that learns optimal execution or dynamic portfolio allocation in high-dimensional, stochastic environments (like order book dynamics) could benefit significantly from such uncertainty-aware, efficient learning techniques, especially in low-data or volatile regimes.
title_cn: EfficientTDMPC：用于样本高效连续控制的改进MPC目标函数
summary_cn: 该研究提出了EfficientTDMPC，一种样本高效的基于模型的强化学习方法。其核心在于通过模型集成和引入不确定性惩罚项来提高规划的可靠性。这些技术对训练需要处理高维、随机市场动态的高级交易代理（如最优执行或动态资产配置）具有重要参考价值，尤其是在数据稀疏或高波动性市场环境下，它可以更稳健地学习长期回报策略。

title: Hypergraph Pattern Machine: Compositional Tokenization for Higher-Order Interactions
summary: Hypergraphs model higher-order relations that drive real-world decisions, from drug prescriptions to recommendations. A central structural signal in such data, beyond what pairwise relations can express, is interaction compositionality: whether a higher-order relation is compositional, emergent, or inhibitory with respect to its observed or unobserved sets. In polypharmacy, the regime decides whether a drug should be dropped, kept, or excluded: a compositional drug triple can be safely simplified, an emergent triple requires all drugs jointly, and an inhibitory triple flags a drug that disrupts an existing interaction. However, existing hypergraph learning methods, which merely propagate messages over observed hyperedges, leave this compositional signal unmodeled, allowing dangerous drug combinations to slip through and be misclassified. To this end, we propose the Hypergraph Pattern Machine (HGPM), shifting the paradigm from message passing to learning the compositional pattern of subsets. It tokenizes compositional subsets, organizes them in an inclusion DAG, and trains an inclusion-aware Transformer under masked reconstruction. On ten hypergraph benchmarks, HGPM matches or exceeds state-of-the-art methods. Notably, in a real adverse-event prediction case, HGPM correctly identifies the drug addition that inhibits the side effect among feature-identical candidates, a discrimination existing methods cannot make. The code and data are in https://github.com/KryieZhao/HGPM.git.
core_methodology: The Hypergraph Pattern Machine (HGPM) shifts focus from standard hyperedge message passing to explicitly learning the *compositional pattern* of subsets. It tokenizes these compositional subsets, organizes them into an inclusion Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), and trains an inclusion-aware Transformer model using masked reconstruction to understand how higher-order interactions (groups of items) behave as a cohesive unit (compositional, emergent, or inhibitory).
data_sources: The methodology is demonstrated on generalized hypergraph benchmarks, specifically mentioning applications in drug interaction prediction (polypharmacy).
